title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
body: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge. For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation. Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency. Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks ’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences. Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral -operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding. Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization. Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do. Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them. Partners including Aleria , Baseten , Cassava , CoreWeave , Crusoe , DigitalOcean , Firebird , Fireworks, Firmus , G42 , GMI Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Lightning AI, Nebius , Nscale , Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers. Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads. Model and inference services help them put that capacity to use. Agent controls address what applications are allowed to do as they move into production. Explore NVIDIA Cloud Partners for infrastructure and services, and the OpenShell Reference Architecture for agent deployment controls. title: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA
body: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA October 21, 2026 by James McKenna 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To increase productivity, accelerate innovation and create new opportunities for economic growth, Europe’s industrial leaders are tapping NVIDIA CUDA-X and Omniverse libraries , as well as NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron open models, across the engineering and manufacturing lifecycle. Bringing those capabilities together on the factory floor, the NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) is now available in early access on GitHub , providing a path for developers to build and deploy always-on factory manager agents that coordinate work across machines, and specialist agents focused on use cases such as visual inspection, root cause analysis, report generation and fleet management. These agents can connect to frontier models, including NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron, and foundational knowledge including computer-aided design, product lifecycle management, simulation software, and IT and operational technology systems. Building on the FOX blueprint enables the ecosystem to build industrial agents that monitor factory operations in real time, correlate visual findings and machine logs to investigate problems, and coordinate responses. With Cosmos in-context learning, these agents can adapt using examples and documentation, without fine-tuning. Siemens is integrating agents built using FOX into Intelligence Center X, its agentic enterprise system, to help identify root causes and coordinate factory operations, for estimated cost savings of 20%. Siemens’ Process Preparation X agents use NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory tools and skills to generate defect images for circuit-board inspection. At its Erlangen electronics factory, Siemens used this approach to reduce calibration time of inspection processes by 40%. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Accelerating Engineering From the First Design NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries accelerate simulation, giving engineers faster feedback to explore design alternatives before committing to physical prototypes. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is releasing cuDSS for general availability , accelerating the demanding calculations behind the complex simulations of structural stress, fluid flow, electromagnetic fields and semiconductor device behavior. Mercedes-Benz uses Siemens’ Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on NVIDIA GPUs to compare vehicle designs through faster aerodynamic simulations. In factories, the company applies NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and the Metropolis VSS blueprint to build agents for vehicle inspection and windshield assembly verification, detecting deviations and ensuring consistently high quality. Cadence is benchmarking automotive fluid-dynamics workloads on NVIDIA GPUs to assess opportunities for faster design iteration, while Autodesk brings the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and Warp frameworks into NavPack, integrated with Autodesk Alias, to help designers like those at Bentley’s predict vehicle performance and iterate faster using simulation-trained AI. imec and Infineon are accelerating semiconductor simulation with Synopsys software and NVIDIA accelerated computing. Benchmarks of S-Litho on imec’s model show up to 40x speedup, while Infineon uses Sentaurus Device with NVIDIA CUDA libraries to achieve a 12x speedup in 3D breakdown simulation for next-generation power devices. Leonardo is working with Neural Concept on AI-driven aircraft design, tapping NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bring aircraft geometry and aerodynamic simulation results together. Video courtesy of Neural Concept and Leonardo. Car manufacturers use Dassault Systèmes ’ LEO & AURA Virtual Companions, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, and orchestrating CATIA AI Agents & SIMULIA AI Agents with SIMULIA solvers, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, to rapidly design and virtually test vehicle doors before building physical prototypes. UniversalAGI is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea. PhysicsX is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team , on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while Fermioniq ’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp. Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models. Testing Factories and Robots Virtually NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable digital twins and robotics simulation , helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor. Video courtesy of Agile Robots, Audi and Dassault Systèmes. Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and Agile Robots to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and  logistics processes in DELMIA virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing. At Volkswagen Sachsen’s Transparent Factory, Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim , built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots. Falkor , a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries. Video courtesy of Falkor, a KONGSBERG company. The same simulation approach extends to AI infrastructure. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA , is developing an AI factory digital twin built for Nscale with Omniverse libraries to help engineers compare power, cooling and equipment configurations before making physical changes. Explore NVIDIA technologies for industrial AI . UniversalAGI is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea. PhysicsX is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team , on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while Fermioniq ’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp. Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models. Testing Factories and Robots Virtually NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable digital twins and robotics simulation , helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor. Video courtesy of Agile Robots, Audi and Dassault Systèmes. Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and Agile Robots to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and  logistics processes in DELMIA virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing. At Volkswagen Sachsen’s Transparent Factory, Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim , built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots. Falkor , a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries. Video courtesy of Falkor, a KONGSBERG company. The same simulation approach extends to AI infrastructure. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA , is developing an AI factory digital twin built for Nscale with Omniverse libraries to help engineers compare power, cooling and equipment configurations before making physical changes. title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations
body: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations October 21, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster. Dassault Systèmes : Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries. Siemens : Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows. Synopsys : Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster. Accelerated Simulation at Scale As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters. Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++,  Python and Fortran interfaces. Learn more about cuDSS by visiting the NVIDIA demo booth and Dassault Systèmes booth at GTC Berlin. Featured image courtesy of Dassault Systèmes. title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
body: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure New Confidential Bare Metal with NVIDIA Confidential Computing protects models and data across cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure — plus, NVIDIA Confidential Computing is expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems as well as NVIDIA DSX OS. October 21, 2026 by John Fanelli 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack . The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today , is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running. Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data. NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options: Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories. Model Builders Tap Global Capacity Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide. Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution. “Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.” Google Cloud is extending support for  Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property. “Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud. Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution. Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems. CoreWeave , Firmus , GMI Cloud , Google Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius , Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems . NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads. Learn more about NVIDIA Confidential Computing . title: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data
body: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data October 21, 2026 by Erik Pounds 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Agents are only as useful as what they know, and only as trustworthy as the boundaries they run within. Leading enterprises are using the open source NVIDIA Agent Toolkit — now expanded with new tools — to customize and control agents, use company data to inform their answers and actions, monitor what they do and govern how they operate. NVIDIA Agent Toolkit comprises: The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation with NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries NVIDIA open models including Nemotron Retriever and the new Kumo family NVIDIA OpenShell secure agent runtime NVIDIA NemoClaw secure agent blueprints Tools and skills, like NeMo Relay and NeMo Compass Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements To develop agents that accomplish real work and are trustworthy from development to deployment, builders need an open agent stack that brings together the models, harness, runtime, data and tools. NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation helps enterprises turn data into company intelligence agents can use. Agents can find relevant information, understand what it means for the business and use it to make predictions and help people decide what to do next. Companies can use Agent Knowledge Foundation without moving data, rebuilding existing workflows or changing governance controls. The foundation features NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries , including cuDF, cuGraph, cuML, cuOpt and cuVS, and the new Auto-Ontology library, which translates raw company data into familiar business concepts — like customers, products and orders — and maps how they relate. It also includes NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever and Kumo Structured open models — Kumo Tabular, Kumo Relational, Kumo Time Series and Kumo Forecast — which help agents find relevant company information to answer questions and make predictions. OpenShell provides the secure runtime boundary, giving enterprises control over what agents can access and do. NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints provide reference designs for building secure, specialized agents. The newest NemoClaw blueprint for agent optimization provides a step-by-step starting point for improving agent intelligence — making them better at their jobs over time. Enterprises Adopt NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation The new NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation is already at work across enterprises. With Palantir , NVIDIA’s supply chain organization is using Agent Knowledge Foundation through Palantir Foundry, Ontology and AIP to deploy specialized agents, create actionable intelligence from proprietary data, predict outcomes and optimize decision-making. Databricks pairs NVIDIA Kumo Anomaly with Databricks Genie Ontology to power context-aware agents. Snowflake is enabling customers to use the NVIDIA Kumo Engine and Kumo Relational open models in their Snowflake Notebook environments to unlock more predictive capabilities. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models make search faster and more accurate. Using the embedding model, Amazon OpenSearch Service improved relevance with fewer search steps and virtually no added latency. SAP ’s fine-tuned reranker ran nearly 3x faster. ServiceNow improved reranking quality while cutting latency by nearly a quarter. Zoom is using Nemotron Retriever models to improve document understanding, search relevance and context retrieval for Zoom AI Services. Amazon Web Services (AWS) , ClickHouse , Cloudera , Cohesity , Dassault Systèmes , Dell , Elastic , Exa , IBM , NetApp , Oracle , Perplexity , Starburst and VAST Data are also among those building on Agent Knowledge Foundation. Learn more by joining this GTC Berlin session on building, deploying and optimizing specialized agents in production . title: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries
body: NVIDIA Open Models Advance Europe’s Sovereign Intelligence Across Industries New model families for vision and language, retrieval, tabular data, biology, robotics and quantum computing supercharge development in Europe. October 21, 2026 by Kari Briski 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is expanding its family of open models across language, robotics, biology, and quantum computing, giving developers, researchers and enterprises what they need to build applications tailored to local languages and industries The portfolio includes the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt models; new NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models for embedding, reranking and document parsing; the new NVIDIA Kumo family open weight foundation models and libraries for structured business data; NVIDIA Cosmos 3.5 world models; NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge for autonomous vehicles; NVIDIA BioNeMo for healthcare and scientific discovery; and NVIDIA Ising for quantum computing. The open models give organizations a foundation they can customize with local data and deploy on infrastructure they control. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA Nemotron Powers Post-Training Across Industries NVIDIA Nemotron brings open language models, datasets and recipes to developers building agents. The models support text and images, helping agents orchestrate workflows, reason through complex problems and complete specialized tasks at a lower cost. Nemotron models are built with data, research and expertise from the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition , including European partners Black Forest Labs , H-Company and Mistral . Nemotron provides a foundation for enterprises to build applications based on their own knowledge and expertise. Dassault Systèmes , Domyn , Dream , Palantir’s customers , Salesforce , SAP , Shopify , Synopsys and WPP , as well as professional services providers like Accenture and EY, are working with Nemotron models and datasets to create custom models and build domain-specific agents. A broad ecosystem of post-training partners, including AfterQuery , AgileRL , AI21 , Alice , Applied Compute , Baseten , CoreWeave , Distil Labs , EON , Fastino , Fireworks , Google Cloud, Mercor , Multiverse Computing , Nebius , Handshake AI , Plurai , Prime Intellect , River.AI, Scale AI , Trajectory and TNG, is helping enterprises customize Nemotron for domain-specific workloads. NVIDIA Kumo Speeds Agents’ Work With Structured Enterprise Data NVIDIA Kumo open foundation models, libraries and tools help agents and applications forecast outcomes, score fraud risk and recommend actions from structured business data. Part of NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation , Kumo shortens time to prediction and reduces the cost and complexity of building a separate machine learning pipeline for every task. Developers can use pretrained Kumo models to bring predictions to more applications quickly, then fine-tune them using proprietary data when higher performance is critical. The portfolio includes NVIDIA Kumo Structured , with models for relational and tabular prediction, forecasting and anomaly detection, and NVIDIA Kumo Engine , an open library stack for developing and deploying structured data foundation models. Cognite , Coinbase , Databricks , DoorDash , Revolut and Tubi are among the first to work with Kumo models to accelerate development. Snowflake customers are already using Kumo models to accelerate AI development in industries including advertising, energy, financial services and retail. NVIDIA Cosmos Accelerates Robotics Training and Simulation NVIDIA Cosmos is a family of open world foundation models that helps developers build robots, autonomous vehicles and vision agents that understand and interact with the physical world. NVIDIA is introducing new Cosmos post-training and optimization tools to help developers improve world models using less compute, along with simulation checkpoints for evaluating behavior in interactive driving and robotic manipulation scenarios before real-world testing. NVIDIA is also introducing Cosmos Data Factory — comprising blueprints and core agent skills — to help developers curate, label, generate and evaluate training data for driving scenarios, product defects, image augmentation and event generation. Developers can use complete workflows or individual capabilities with agents coordinating the process. Porsche with Voxel51 , ANYbotics with Encord , Zalando and CEVA Logistics with Sereact , and Siemens are using Cosmos Data Factory to create high-quality, diverse training datasets and improve model precision. NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Brings Real-Time Reasoning to Autonomous Vehicles NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge is a compact reasoning model that brings real-time scene understanding and motion planning directly into autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos and optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor platform, it helps developers bring advanced driving capabilities into vehicles with lower computing requirements. NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina Advances Protein Design NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina is an open protein design model from NVIDIA and the Baker Lab at the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design. The model generates protein sequences and 3D structures to help researchers design proteins that bind to difficult targets, assemble into complex structures and bind to small molecules. NVIDIA BioNeMo RFD4-Proteina delivers leading performance across more than 10 protein design tasks and generates designs about 13x faster than RFdiffusion3 in a benchmark of 200 amino acid proteins. Researchers can use the model through agents to generate and evaluate candidates against design goals and molecular constraints, then choose which designs to test in the lab. NVIDIA Ising Accelerates Quantum Development The NVIDIA Ising family of open models provides a common, extensible foundation to speed the breakthroughs needed to develop useful quantum supercomputers, from real-time hardware calibration to error correction, across different qubit modalities and tailored to individual hardware needs. IQM Quantum Computers is using Ising to calibrate its quantum processors, showcasing how specialized open calibration models outperform large general-purpose models. SEEQC is combining the NVIDIA NVQLink platform and Ising with its unique Digital Link to meet the low-latency requirements needed for real-time quantum error correction. AWS is making NVIDIA Ising readily available to researchers by integrating the model family into AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS). While decoding is typically performed on classical hardware colocated with the quantum processor due to latency requirements, the AWS PCS integration lets researchers build on Ising prior to deployment. Availability NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available on Hugging Face , ModelScope , OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as through NVIDIA cloud, post-training and inference partners. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is expected to be available on Friday, Oct. 23. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever open models are available on Hugging Face , various partner platforms, and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice on build.nvidia.com . NVIDIA Kumo open models are available on Hugging Face and optimized and packaged as an NVIDIA NIM microservice for production inference on build.nvidia.com . NVIDIA Cosmos is now openly available on Hugging Face and GitHub , and through select inference partners. NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge will be available for download on GitHub and Hugging Face later this month. The NVIDIA BioNeMo open model RFD4-Proteina is available on build.nvidia.com and as an NVIDIA NIM microservice, as well as on GitHub, Hugging Face and through select inference partners. NVIDIA Ising is available on GitHub, Hugging Face and build.nvidia.com . See notice regarding software product information. title: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote
body: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote October 21, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events. Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle. GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements AI is a five-layer cake , Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application. “Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid. “To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.” The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure. “This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.” He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings. Next, Huang announced NVIDIA DSX POD , a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready. “This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.” The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power. Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful. He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools. “The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored. NVIDIA’s answer is the new NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents , a full-stack design built on NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect. That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said. Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage Huang presented NVIDIA’s open models as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs. NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI. “We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.” NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.” “You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.” NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer Huang then introduced the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases. He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new NVIDIA Kumo models for making predictions from structured data. “Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said. NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents Huang then described NVIDIA CUDA-X as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it. Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work. “CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said. Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering A video showcased NVIDIA Agent Toolkit bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples: At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab. At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor. And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design. “And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.” Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure. He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia after nearly eight years of work. “Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. It will enhance our spectrum efficiency tremendously.” AI Moves Into the Treatment Room Healthcare and life sciences leaders are building on NVIDIA technologies to advance drug discovery and expand patient care. For example, NVIDIA and Siemens Healthineers are developing AI-enabled radiation therapy. Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves. Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting. “The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.” The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem Huang said the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets , with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services. Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets. In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles at scale. Volkswagen’s van, JLR, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz’s next-generation vehicles will be Hyperion-compatible, Huang announced, saying, “Welcome to Hyperion.” A Reference Humanoid for Robotics Researchers Huang then announced Agile ONE SN , a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days. The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components. “This is a great starting point,” Huang said. Every company in Europe will become an AI company … and we’re going to have a thriving AI economy here in Europe.” To close, Huang had one more surprise: a Eurovision-style musical send-off that turned the keynote’s themes into a comic recap. The lyrics raced from OpenShell’s guardrails — “No credentials. Access dismissed” and “Sentry on BlueField never clocks off” — to physical AI, where robot training was likened to “college for robots without student loans.” The punchline: “You can’t spell fungible without fun.” A saxophone solo led into a rousing “We are Europa” chorus. “Let’s work together to build Europe’s AI economy and put AI to work,” Huang said, closing out his talk. “Have a great GTC.” Explore NVIDIA GTC Berlin blogs and press releases in the online press kit . retained_feed_body: Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events. Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle. GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements AI is a five-layer cake , Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application. “Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid. “To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.” The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure. “This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.” He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings. Next, Huang announced NVIDIA DSX POD , a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready. “This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.” The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power. Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful. He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools. “The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored. NVIDIA’s answer is the new NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents , a full-stack design built on NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect. That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said. Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage Huang presented NVIDIA’s open models as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs. NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI. “We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.” NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.” “You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.” NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer Huang then introduced the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases. He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new NVIDIA Kumo models for making predictions from structured data. “Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said. NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents Huang then described NVIDIA CUDA-X as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it. Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work. “CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said. Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering A video showcased NVIDIA Agent Toolkit bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples: At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab. At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor. And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design. “And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.” Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure. He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia after nearly eight years of work. “Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves. Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting. “The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.” The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem Huang said the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets , with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services.
